[LGRA.2.9.6.2] `interp_body`'s leading `NAME` resolves to any
**in-scope value-binding** — an LHS pattern binding, a `const`, a
series companion, or a `let` (pure **or sync-impure**, e.g. a `let`
bound to `now()` or `cached("k")`) — and interpolation formats that
**bound value**; the `('.'NAME | '['INT_LIT']')*` tail applies to the
value. A dotted body resolves as a dotted name in expression position does
([LGRA.22.9]), so `{lib.CONST}` formats the constant `CONST` of an imported
library `lib`, a `const` like the file's own. A `let`'s RHS purity is irrelevant to interpolability: a
sync-impure `let` is bound once per activation ([LGRA.9.8.4]), so its
captured value formats deterministically. The body is a **name/path,
not an inline expression** — an inline call or operator (`{now()}`,
`{cached("k")}`, `{c.a + c.b}`) is a compile error ([LGRA.2.9.6.9]). An
unknown binding is a compile error; a null / absent bound value (e.g. a
`cached` miss) renders as the **empty string**.
